title: Strategist Weighs September Fed Hike Amid Mixed Data
summary:
Laureline Renaud-Chatelain, fixed income strategy lead at Pictet Wealth Management, discussed the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September. She noted that the recent payroll data was somewhat surprising but indicated a stable labor market that is not adding inflationary pressure. Despite noisy and downwardly revised employment figures, the key focus remains on upcoming Consumer Price Index (CPI) prints, which will heavily influence the Fed's decision.

(Corrects name of guest in video). (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Advances as Traders Watch US Inflation for Rate-Hike Clues
summary: Gold advanced, as traders weighed prospects for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while awaiting US inflation data for clues on the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.

title: Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran Resigns Ahead of AGM Next Week
summary: Natarajan Chandrasekaran will step down as chairman of Tata Sons Pvt. when his term ends in February 2027, deepening a leadership crisis at the Indian conglomerate at a time when it’s spearheading the country’s push into high-tech sectors.

title: US Stock Futures Climb Before Key Inflation Print: Markets Wrap
summary: Equity futures advanced as upbeat results from AI infrastructure firms revived appetite for tech stocks with traders awaiting a key US inflation reading later Wednesday.

title: Most Electricity Sought for AI Data Centers in US Will Never Materialize
summary: More than two-thirds of the electricity sought for the artificial intelligence boom in the US isn’t likely to materialize due to “phantom” projects and long-shot pitches.

title: UAE Shuttles Iraqi Oil Exports Through the Strait of Hormuz
summary: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co.’s trading arm is offering to shuttle exports of Iraqi oil through the Strait of Hormuz, using its dark-transit playbook to transport Basrah and other crude to refiners in Asia, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Why Romantasy May Soon Be a Billion-Dollar Business
summary: Romantasy has grown from a BookTok-driven obsession to a nearly billion-dollar business, powered by a largely female fandom scooping up special editions, merchandise, event tickets, audiobooks and more. The genre's rise is reshaping publishing and drawing retailers, creators and now Hollywood into one of the book industry’s most powerful new markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Pimco Sees Fed on Hold Through 2026 as Inflation Moderates
summary: Marc Seidner, CIO for non-traditional strategies at Pimco, discusses the outlook for inflation, the US economy and Federal Reserve policy. "We're much less fussed about about the inflation outlook on a forward-looking basis than I think many in the market," Seidner tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Pimco’s Seidner Says Angst Over Fed Credibility is Unwarranted
summary: Pacific Investment Management Co. says market anxiety about the inflation-fighting credentials of the Federal Reserve is overdone and that US bond yields at current levels look attractive.

title: Lloyds Metals Allowed to Ready Restart of Giant PNG Copper Mine
summary: An Indian iron ore producer was authorized to work toward restarting a giant Papua New Guinea copper mine that’s been closed for almost 40 years and was once a flash point in a brutal civil war.

title: Yen Intervention Put China’s Yuan Under More Pressure, BE Says
summary: China’s currency has come under more pressure to appreciate since the US and Japan moved to strengthen the yen, according to Bloomberg Economics, potentially draining support for growth as the yuan gains despite falling bond yields and a sluggish economy.

title: Korea to Require Mock Trading for Single-Stock Leveraged ETFs
summary: South Korea will require new investors in single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds to undergo mock trading exercises, further tightening rules on highly risky products that have amplified market volatility.

title: JPY/USD: Why Yen Intervention by Japan and US Has Limited Impact
summary: The yen’s weakness has become a growing issue for Japan’s policymakers, given its role in driving up import prices and household living costs. It’s also become a worry for the US.

title: Solar Eclipse to Flip the Off Switch on Europe’s Solar Farms
summary: Night will fall on Europe’s power system a bit early Wednesday evening, as an eclipse is set to block solar generation across parts of the UK and western Europe.

title: Machinery Maker DMG Mori Seeks $300 Million in Japan Share Sale
summary: DMG Mori Co. is aiming to raise ¥48.2 billion ($302 million) through the sale of new shares in the overseas markets as global investors show solid appetite for the nation’s stocks.

title: SK Hynix, Samsung Shares Gain as Report Says Temasek to Invest
summary: South Korean chipmakers rallied as risk appetite returned after last month’s rout and traders weighed a local media report that Singapore’s Temasek Holdings Pte plans to invest in Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc.

title: Heatwave Slams Europe Straining Energy Supply, E.On CEO Says
summary:
As Europe is hit by its fifth heatwave, the continent's largest energy provider joins Bloomberg's Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie on 'The Opening Trade'. "We see massive increases in wholesale prices because of the Persian Gulf. We've seen extremely high gas prices putting stress on customers and affordability. Right now we see a very hot summer curtailing output that will lead to short-term distortions. We need to continue but it's stressful."
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Shoprite Jumps as E-Commerce Boom Boosts Full-Year Profit
summary: Shoprite Holdings Ltd. climbed the most in 11 months as Africa’s largest supermarket chain said it sees earnings rising as much as 14.7% because of higher sales at its e-commerce unit.
